25944-essentials-of-diseases-of-the-skin.creator: Henry W. Stelwagon, M.D., Ph.D.
25944-essentials-of-diseases-of-the-skin.description: A book by Henry W. Stelwagon, M.D., Ph.D.. This book contains #double the material in the ordinary students' dictionary#, and yet, by the use of a clear, condensed type and thin paper of the finest quality, is only 1-3/4 inches in thickness. It is bound in full flexible leather, and is just the kind of a book that a man will want to keep on his desk for constant reference.

8300-the-bible-douay-rheims-complete-the.title: The Bible Douay Rheims Complete The Challoner Revision
8300-the-bible-douay-rheims-complete-the.creator: Unknown
8300-the-bible-douay-rheims-complete-the.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. ligious and scholarly adherence to the Latin Vulgate text led to the less elegant and idiomatic words and phrases often found in the translation. In some instances where no English word conveyed the full meaning of the Latin, a Latin word was Anglicized and its meaning defined in a glossary. Although ridiculed by critics, many of these words later found common usage in the English language.

arxiv-2008-04739.title: Mean-Field Theory of Inhomogeneous Fluids
arxiv-2008-04739.creator: S.M. Tschopp, H.D. Vuijk, A. Sharma, J.M. Brader
arxiv-2008-04739.description: Abstract The Barker-Henderson perturbation theory is a bedrock of liquid-state physics, providing quantitative predictions for the bulk thermodynamic properties of realistic model systems. However, this successful method has not been exploited for the study of inhomogeneous systems. We develop and implement a first-principles ‘Barker-Henderson density functional’, thus providing a robust and quantitatively accurate theory for classical fluids in external fields.

arxiv-2109-07675.title: Formation of a strong negative wake behind a helical swimmer in a viscoelastic fluid
arxiv-2109-07675.creator: Shijian Wu 1, Tomas Solano 2, Kourosh Shoele 2, Hadi Mohammadigoushki 1
arxiv-2109-07675.description: Abstract We investigate the effects of helical swimmer shape (i.e., helical pitch angle and tail thickness) on swimming dynamics in a constant viscosity viscoelastic (Boger) fluid via a combination of particle tracking velocimetry, particle image velocimetry and 3D simulations of the FENE-P model. The 3D printed helical swimmer is actuated in a magnetic field using a custom-built rotating Helmholtz coil.

arxiv-2109-09541.title: Scaling TensorFlow to 300 million predictions per second Conference: Fifteenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems; September 27-October 1, 2021; Amsterdam, Netherlands Fifteenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys ’21), September 27-October 1, 2021, Amsterdam, Netherlands DOI: 10.1145/3
arxiv-2109-09541.creator: Jan Hartman, Davorin Kopič
arxiv-2109-09541.description: Abstract . We present the process of transitioning machine learning models to the TensorFlow framework at a large scale in an online advertising ecosystem. In this talk we address the key challenges we faced and describe how we successfully tackled them; notably, implementing the models in TF and serving them efficiently with low latency using various optimization techniques.

arxiv-2112-08304.title: On the Convergence and Robustness of Adversarial Training
arxiv-2112-08304.creator: Yisen Wang, Xingjun Ma, James Bailey, Jinfeng Yi, Bowen Zhou, Quanquan Gu
arxiv-2112-08304.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yisen Wang, Xingjun Ma, James Bailey, Jinfeng Yi, Bowen Zhou, Quanquan Gu. Improving the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs) to adversarial examples is an important yet challenging problem for secure deep learning. Across existing defense techniques, adversarial training with Projected Gradient Decent (PGD) is amongst the most effective.

arxiv-2202-07420.title: Efficient separation of quantum from classical correlations for mixed states with a fixed charge
arxiv-2202-07420.creator: Christian Carisch, Oded Zilberberg
arxiv-2202-07420.description: Abstract Entanglement is the key resource for quantum technologies and is at the root of exciting many-body phenomena. However, quantifying the entanglement between two parts of a real-world quantum system is challenging when it interacts with its environment, as the latter mixes cross-boundary classical with quantum correlations.

arxiv-2206-04807.title: Hybrid electroluminescent devices composed of (In,Ga)N micro-LEDs and monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides
arxiv-2206-04807.creator: K. Oreszczuk 1 , J. Slawinska 2 , A. Rodek 1 , M. Potemski 1,3 , C. Skierbiszewski 2 , and P. Kossacki 1
arxiv-2206-04807.description: Abstract We demonstrate a novel electro-luminescence device in which GaN-based μ \upmu -LEDs are used to trigger the emission spectra of monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides, which are deposited directly on μ \upmu -LED surface. A special μ \upmu -LED design enables the operation of our structures even in the limit of low temperatures.

arxiv-2307-16664.title: Generative models for wearables data
arxiv-2307-16664.creator: Arinbjörn Kolbeinsson, Luca Foschini
arxiv-2307-16664.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arinbjörn Kolbeinsson, Luca Foschini. Data scarcity is a common obstacle in medical research due to the high costs associated with data collection and the complexity of gaining access to and utilizing data. Synthesizing health data may provide an efficient and cost-effective solution to this shortage, enabling researchers to explore distributions and populations that are not represented in existing observations or difficult to access due to privacy considerations. To that end, we have developed a multi-task self-attention model that produces realistic wearable activity data.

arxiv-2308-14438.title: Freeze-in bino dark matter in high scale supersymmetry
arxiv-2308-14438.creator: Mengchao Zhang
arxiv-2308-14438.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mengchao Zhang. We explore a scenario of high scale supersymmetry where all supersymmetric particles except gauginos stay at a high energy scale M SUSY M_{\rm SUSY} which is much larger than the reheating temperature T RH T_{\text{RH}} . The dark matter is dominated by bino component with mass around the electroweak scale and the observed relic abundance is mainly generated by the freeze-in process during the early universe.

arxiv-2407-12928.title: On the representation of number-theoretic functions by arithmetic terms
arxiv-2407-12928.creator: Mihai Prunescu, Lorenzo Sauras-Altuzarra
arxiv-2407-12928.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mihai Prunescu, Lorenzo Sauras-Altuzarra. We present closed forms for several functions that are fundamental in number theory and we explain the method used to obtain them. Concretely, we find formulas for the p p -adic valuation, the number-of-divisors function, the sum-of-divisors function, Euler’s totient function, the modular inverse, the integer part of the root, the integer part of the logarithm, the multiplicative order and the discrete logarithm.

arxiv-2407-19842.title: Detecting and Understanding Vulnerabilities in Language Models via Mechanistic Interpretability
arxiv-2407-19842.creator: Jorge García-Carrasco, Alejandro Maté, Juan Trujillo
arxiv-2407-19842.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs), characterized by being trained on broad amounts of data in a self-supervised manner, have shown impressive performance across a wide range of tasks. Indeed, their generative abilities have aroused interest on the application of LLMs across a wide range of contexts.

arxiv-2412-07450.title: Direct phase encoding in QAOA: Describing combinatorial optimization problems through binary decision variables Thanks: This work has been supported by the Ministry of Economic Affairs Baden-Württemberg in the project SEQUOIA under project number 036-840012.
arxiv-2412-07450.creator: Simon Garhofer*, Oliver Bringmann
arxiv-2412-07450.description: Abstract The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and its derived variants are widely in use for approximating combinatorial optimization problem instances on gate-based Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) computers. Commonly, circuits required for QAOA are constructed by first reformulating a given problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem.

arxiv-2508-01553.title: How Many Times Do People Usually Experience Different Kinds of Stressors Each Day? Conference: Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing; October 12–16, 2025; Espoo, Finland Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and
arxiv-2508-01553.creator: Sameer Neupane, Mithun Saha, David M. Almeida, Santosh Kumar
arxiv-2508-01553.description: Abstract . Understanding how frequently people experience different kinds of daily stressors is crucial for interpreting stress exposure and informing mental health care. But it can’t be directly estimated from current assessment methods, such as diaries, end-of-day interviews, and ecological momentary assessments (EMA), that use sparse sampling to limit participant burden, and a structured response format for uniformity.

arxiv-2509-00821.title: Nonclassical correlations and quadrature squeezing of photons in anisotropic quantum Rabi-Stark model
arxiv-2509-00821.creator: Yong-Xin Zhang 1, Chen Wang 2,, Qing-Hu Chen 1,3,
arxiv-2509-00821.description: Abstract This study investigates nonclassical effects of photons in the anisotropic quantum Rabi-Stark model by using a quantum dressed master equation. We analyze second- and higher-order correlation functions, and demonstrate that the nonlinear Stark coupling significantly modulates photon statistics, inducing distinct and tunable photon antibunching and bunching effects.

pmc-10581340.title: Editorial: A year in review: discussions in cellular endocrinology
pmc-10581340.creator: Damian G. Romero, Pieter de Lange
pmc-10581340.description: search Topic. The review by Wan et al. entitled “Stem Cell Transplantation in the Treatment of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: From Insulin Replacement to Beta-Cell Replacement” discusses the recent advances in stem cell transplantation for the treatment of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM). More than half a billion adults live with Diabetes Mellitus (DM) worldwide (1).

pmc-11520274.title: The Effect of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on M1 with and without Mirror Visual Feedback on Range of Motion and Hand Grip Strength of the Affected Upper Limb in Children with Spastic Hemiplegic Cerebral Palsy
pmc-11520274.creator: Pegah Farzamfar, Ali Heirani, Ehsan Amiri, Mustafa Sedighi, Daniel Gomes da Silva Machado
pmc-11520274.description: ObjectivesThis study investigated the effects of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) before and during the mirror visual feedback (MVF) on hand grip strength (HGS) and range of motion of the affected hand in children with spastic hemiplegia cerebral palsy (SHCP).Materials & MethodsTwelve children with SHCP participated in this randomized, crossover, and double-blind study.

pmc-12618248.title: Heterologous two-dose Ebola vaccine regimen in pregnant women in Rwanda: a randomized controlled phase 3 trial
pmc-12618248.creator: Julien Nyombayire, Rosine Ingabire, Amelia Mazzei, Tyronza Sharkey, Claudine Umuhoza, Jeannine Mukamuyango, Susan Allen, Amanda Tichacek, Rachel Parker, Kristin M. Wall, Michael Katwere, Babajide Keshinro, Auguste Gaddah, Yan Wang, Chiara A. Forcheh, Chelsea McLean, Valérie Oriol-Mathieu, Kerstin Lu
pmc-12618248.description: Risk of death for both mother and fetus following Ebola virus infection is extremely high. In this study, healthy women in Rwanda aged ≥18 years were randomized to two-dose Ebola vaccination (Ad26.ZEBOV, MVA-BN-Filo) during pregnancy (group A) or postpartum (group B). Unvaccinated pregnant group B women served as control.

pmc-13071790.title: Declining Ecosystem Respiration Linked to Nitrogen Deposition: Insights From a 26‐Year FLUXNET Record
pmc-13071790.creator: Michiel K van der Molen, Marnix van de Sande, Michiel in 't Zandt, Tori Saccomandi, Sophie L Baartman, Hong Zhao, Jordi Vilà‐Guerau de Arellano
pmc-13071790.description: Long‐term carbon flux measurements at the FLUXNET site Loobos, a Pine forest in the Netherlands, reveal a counter‐intuitive decline in total ecosystem respiration (TER) by tens of percents between 1997 and 2021. This trend cannot be explained by temperature variability or methodological changes alone.

pmc-13288482.title: Lock out: targeting TMPRSS2 to block influenza and coronaviruses
pmc-13288482.creator: Lu Zhang, Markus Hoffmann, Stefan Pöhlmann
pmc-13288482.description: Coronaviruses and influenza A viruses (IAV) can cause severe respiratory disease and have pandemic potential. Both viruses depend on priming of their glycoproteins by host cell proteases for the acquisition of infectivity, and the responsible enzymes represent potential targets for intervention. Initial studies suggested that these viruses may exploit redundant proteolytic systems.

pmc-13294454.title: The next generation of alginate dressings: recent innovations for chronic wound healing
pmc-13294454.creator: Eduarda Pinto, Cristina C Barrias, Judite Novais Barbosa
pmc-13294454.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chronic wounds remain a major clinical challenge with a huge associated socioeconomic burden. Therefore, multifunctional biomaterials that can simultaneously manage exudate, modulate inflammation, prevent infection and promote tissue regeneration are extremely needed. Alginate, a naturally derived and highly biocompatible polysaccharide, has long been used in the clinic for advanced wound care due to its intrinsic gel-forming ability and capacity to maintain a moist healing environment.
